text.p: Greek Viossol building materials company told institutional investors on Wednesday its estimated pretax profit for 1996 was 568 million drachmas, up 51.4 percent from 375 million in 1995.
It forecast 1997 pretax profit would drop 33.4 percent to 378 million drachmas. In 1998 the company expects profits will rise 12.6 percent to 426 million.
Viossol estimated 1996 turnover at 2,580 billion drachmas, up 3.4 percent from 2,494 billion in 1995.
It specialises in thermal systems, in which it covers 62 percent of the Greek market and air conditioning systems with a 21 percent market share.
It also produces stainless steel sinks, which account for 9 percent of the domestic market and scaffoldings.
